preconditions.description: The dimension n is an integer between 1 and 100 inclusive.
The number of ones k is an integer between 0 and 10^6 inclusive.
Both n and k are integers.

postconditions.expression: max_ones = n * n and (k > max_ones or (k % 2 != 0 and k > n)) implies stdout.strip() == '-1'
postconditions.description: Output is -1 if k exceeds the total number of cells or if k is odd and greater than n (making symmetry impossible).

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() != '-1' implies all(0 <= int(val) <= 1 for row in stdout.strip().split('\n') for val in row.split())
postconditions.description: If a matrix is output, it contains only 0s and 1s.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() != '-1' implies len(stdout.strip().split('\n')) == n and all(len(row.split()) == n for row in stdout.strip().split('\n'))
postconditions.description: If a matrix is output, it has exactly n rows and n columns.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() != '-1' implies all(int(matrix[i][j]) == int(matrix[j][i]) for i in range(n) for j in range(n))
postconditions.description: If a matrix is output, it is symmetric with respect to the main diagonal.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() != '-1' implies sum(sum(int(val) for val in row.split()) for row in stdout.strip().split('\n')) == k
postconditions.description: If a matrix is output, the total count of ones equals k.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() != '-1' implies all((int(matrix[i][j]) == 1) or (int(matrix[i][j]) == 0 and (i > 0 or j > 0)) for i in range(n) for j in range(n))
postconditions.description: The matrix is lexicographically maximal: ones are placed as early as possible (top-left to bottom-right) while respecting symmetry constraints.
